Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking time last week. Attached is an updated mutual action plan (redwood_map_v2.xlsx) and the draft SOW (redwood_draft_sow.pdf) that align to the 3-month evaluation you described. High-level commercial points we want to confirm so we can lock the pilot start date and produce a PO: 

- Pilot scope & ramp: 3-month evaluation, initial allocation 25k tokens/month (baseline), targeted ramp to 225–250k tokens/month by month 4 post-pilot.
- Pricing: pilot unit price $0.0025/token; post-pilot committed tiers available (see MAP). Discounts kick in once a minimum committed monthly cadence is accepted (tiered: 8% @ 6mo commit, 12% @ 12mo commit).
- Invoicing cadence: monthly in arrears is our default.
- Payment terms: we typically run Net30. We can consider Net60 for the first invoice while your PO is processing but prefer Net30 thereafter.
- PO & billing start: we noted you may require the PO before invoices are issued and a billing start date tied to UAT sign-off — please confirm.

Can you confirm procurement details (billing contact, PO lead time, any mandatory PO language) and whether Atlas requires milestone-based invoices tied to the MAP? If you can share the expected PO timeline we can propose a firm billing start that avoids duplicate charges for the pilot ramp period.

I copied Marissa to confirm technical acceptance criteria for UAT so we can align the billing start to either calendar start or signed UAT.

Thanks —

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the docs. A few procurement items to confirm from our side before we issue a PO: 

1) Payment terms — Atlas standard is Net60. Will Redwood accept Net60 for invoices? If possible we prefer Net60 for all invoices; if not, we can accept Net60 for the first invoice while PO is processed, then Net30 thereafter — subject to approval.
2) PO requirement — Procurement requires a PO number before processing any invoice. Please confirm you can place the PO number on all invoices.
3) Billing start trigger — Our legal ops prefers billing to start after UAT sign-off to avoid paying for pre-production work. Can you align the billing start to a UAT completion milestone?
4) Milestone invoicing — We can consider a milestone schedule tied to the MAP (example: 30% on pilot kick-off, 40% at ramp completion, 30% on enterprise rollout readiness) — is Redwood able to invoice against MAP milestones rather than pure monthly usage for the initial purchase?

If you can confirm acceptance of PO-based invoicing and whether Redwood will accept Net60 for the first invoice (or all invoices), we’ll circulate a PO draft to AP (ap@atlasfinancial.com).

Emma —

Wanted to surface a few operational notes from the delivery side so we can close the MAP and lock the dates: 

- Invoicing cadence: We typically invoice monthly in arrears based on measured usage. For customers that require milestone billing we can accommodate a hybrid approach for the pilot: initial milestone invoice (covering onboarding & reserved capacity) followed by monthly usage invoices thereafter.
- PO placement: We fully support PO numbers on invoices. Please indicate the AP contact (you listed ap@atlasfinancial.com). We’ll ensure PO number and your requisition fields appear on every invoice PDF.
- Payment term compromise: Accept Net60 for the first invoice only (to accommodate PO processing). Subsequent invoices would revert to Net30. If Atlas requires Net60 for the full contract term, we need to model that into discounts/commit levels — we can discuss commercial tradeoffs.
- Billing start date options: (A) Calendar start (date the pilot begins) or (B) UAT-signed start. We recommend UAT-signed start to ensure you’re not billed before acceptance; if you choose calendar start, the first invoice will simply reflect pro-rated usage.
- MAP-linked milestone invoicing: We can invoice against MAP milestones for major deliverables, but usage-based charges (tokens) will still be billed monthly in arrears. For the pilot, example proposal: 1) Milestone A (kick-off onboarding) — one-time onboarding invoice; 2) Milestone B (UAT sign-off) — first pro-rated invoice; 3) Milestone C (ramp complete) — adjustment invoice reflecting ramp commit/discount.

Attached is a short MAP summary (map_summary.txt) describing the milestone definitions and a revised ribbon in the spreadsheet to show where discounts apply. If Atlas prefers milestone invoicing only (no monthly usage invoices) we can create a fixed-fee pilot SOW instead — that’s an alternative we can draft quickly.

Happy to hop on a quick call to finalize wording in the PO and confirm the billing contact.

Cheers,

1) Discount & commit tradeoff: We’ll provide a 10% pilot credit (applied as a one-time invoice credit) if Atlas signs a PO within 10 business days and commits to a ramp plan that reaches >=200k tokens/month by month 4. For a longer-term committed contract we can apply the standard tiered discounts (8% for 6-month minimum, 12% for 12-month minimum) as reviewed in the MAP.
2) Payment terms: Redwood accepts the following — Net60 for the first invoice only (to accommodate PO processing); Net30 standard thereafter. If Atlas requires Net60 for the entire term, commercial adjustments will be needed (we can discuss a fee to offset extended payment risk).
3) PO & invoicing: We will accept purchase orders and will include PO numbers on every invoice. We can support milestone invoices for onboarding and ramp payments while continuing monthly usage invoices in arrears for token consumption. Alternatively, we can convert the pilot to a fixed-fee SOW if Atlas prefers no monthly invoices.
